campaign: OpenFront Neural Schema 5 - Vom guten Offline-Modell zum echten Champion

run3Schema4Champion.role: ACTIVE champion (schema-4 planner model); the bar the schema-5 controller must exceed in S10

keyFindings: model score gap (top-1 vs top-2 legal) median ~0.0009, p90 ~0.558: the model is near-degenerate across legal candidates
rule top-2 utility gap (the barrier to flip) median ~31, p90 ~90: a large integer rule-utility wall
requiredGain to flip = ruleGap/modelGap; median ~538, p90 ~1.68e6, max ~5.3e8
requiredGain <= 18 in ~38 frames, <= 60 in ~178 frames, <= 150 in ~477 frames of 1473

conclusion: the bottleneck is model score-entanglement, not only the gain. Raising the gain (B) alone amplifies the near-constant vector; the principled fixes are score->utility calibration (C) and confidence-gated control (G).

invariants: all arms re-order only already-legal candidates; downstream legality (director + planners) stays authoritative
all arms preserve every hard safety check (reserve floors, emergency defense, spawn, capacity)
the gain/mapping is the only degree of freedom; no new action is invented

rule-basis.role: baseline; no neural influence on the bounded candidate pick

run3-schema4.role: baseline; ACTIVE schema-4 planner champion biases the planners (not the candidate control)

A.role: current production candidate control (baseline for the variants)
A.hypothesis: near-identical to rule-basis because the model score is near-degenerate (S1: endLand identical in most scenarios)

B.role: higher raw gain at the documented clamp ceiling (60)
B.hypothesis: flips the ~11% of frames with requiredGain <= 60; tests whether more changes (not better mapping) helps; S5 warns the gain must not simply be maxed, so B is a boundary probe, not the expected winner

C.role: per-frame z-score calibration of the model score before scaling
C.hypothesis: removes the near-constant magnitude so the model's full per-frame ranking is expressed; directly targets the S4 score-entanglement finding

D.role: confidence-scaled gain: 18 when the model is uncertain, up to 60 when its top-1/top-2 margin is high
D.hypothesis: applies more influence only when the model is confident; bounded version of B

E.role: schema-4 planner champion + schema-5 candidate control together
E.hypothesis: combines the planner-level bias (proven to diverge from rule-basis in S1) with the candidate-level control

F.role: scale-free rank mapping: the model's rank position (1..0) becomes the utility bonus
F.hypothesis: discards score magnitude entirely; pure ranking signal, most robust to score-entanglement

G.role: confidence-gated override: the model may only re-order when its top-1 clears the rule top-1 by >= 0.25 AND the implied required gain is within capGain
G.hypothesis: minimal-intervention control; changes the pick only on high-confidence frames; targets the S4 score-entanglement finding while protecting against noise
